## WristClaw v0.1.2 → v0.2.0 changelog

This release tightens security for pairing, switches to an auditable install path, and clarifies delivery rules.

- Explicit user confirmation is now required before pairing any new WristClaw session.
- The default install path is via npm (`@wristclaw/openclaw`); curl/bash script is fallback only, with manual review.
- Added an allowlist for safe relay URLs; custom relays prompt explicit user approval.
- Each pairing now binds the watch's X25519 public key, ensuring only the correct watch resumes the session.
- Documentation clarified for safer pairing, deactivation, and reply delivery practices.
- License, homepage, repository, and category metadata added.

wristclaw 0.1.1

- No code or documentation changes detected in this version.
- Behavior, features, and documentation remain the same as the previous release.

WristClaw 0.1.0 — Initial Release

- Introduces a new bridge skill connecting the WristClaw Apple Watch app with the OpenClaw agent, enabling end-to-end encrypted text, audio, and image delivery directly to the watch.
- Detects and registers pairing payloads sent via Telegram or any channel, supporting both JSON and URL formats.
- Automates setup: installs the native WristClaw OpenClaw channel and registers pairing sessions with concise, user-friendly confirmation.
- Streamlines reply routing, ensuring all wrist replies go only through stdout (never secondary channels) for a consistent watch experience.
- Supports rich, context-aware replies with full skill access and ambient signals; emphasizes clarity and brevity in watch responses.
